d: Install Nostr Vault on an iPhone or iPad, create a Nostr account or bring the one you have, and find your way around.
h: Install · Pick a way in · Create an account · Bring the account you have · Who told you about Nostr Vault? · Find your way around · Next
x: Nostr Vault runs your own Nostr relay on your phone. Your posts, messages and media are kept on the phone, and copies go out to public relays so people can see them. Install Nostr Vault needs iOS 17 or later, on an iPhone or an iPad. Join the beta on TestFlight , install it, and open it. The first screen on iPhone Pick a way in The first screen has two buttons. What's inside? under them lists what the app does. Create an account if you're new to Nostr. You get a new key, a password for it and a profile. I already use Nostr if you have an account from another Nostr app. You bring that account, and your old notes come home to your phone. Create an account Welcome to Nostr. A short explanation of Nostr and your vault. Tap Create My Account . Your Keys. Two keys replace a username and password. The public key is your name on Nostr; share it freely. The secret key is your password; anyone who has it can post as you. Tap Copy next to the secret key and save it in your password manager. Nobody can recover it for you. Tick I saved my secret key , then Continue . Protect Your Key. Choose a password of at least 8 characters. This password locks the secret key you just saved. It stays on this device only and is never sent to us or any server. We cannot recover or reset it. If you forget it, the secret key you saved is your only way back in. Write it down and keep it with your secret key. Your Profile. Add a photo and a name, or tap Skip for Now . You can change both later. Welcome to Nostr! Your account is made and your relay is running. Tap Start Exploring . Fill your feed. Nostr starts empty: no algorithm picks for you. Tap Let's fill it , pick a few topics, and follow people whose posts you like. Five follows build your web of trust, which fills your feed and filters out spam. Not now skips it. Your Keys (secret key hidden here) Protect Your Key Your Profile Fill your feed You're done when your Following feed shows posts from the people you followed. Bring the account you have Tap I already use Nostr . The screen asks Who are you on Nostr? Paste one of these into the box, or tap Scan your key or signer link to scan a QR code. The app tells you what you'll be able to do: You paste The app shows What you get Your npub, or name@domain Read-only Your feed, notes and follows. Add your secret key later in Settings to post. Your nsec (secret key) You can post Post, reply, DM and zap. You choose a password, and the key is saved encrypted on this phone. It's never sent anywhere. An ncryptsec (a key locked with a password) Encrypted key · you can post Enter the password you locked it with. A bunker:// link from a signer app Signer link · you can post Your signer app approves each post. Your key never touches Nostr Vault. To use a signer app instead, tap Use a signer app , then Sign in with Clave . See Signers . Checking your relays. The app looks for your notes on your relays. Tap Start import . Bringing your notes home. A few cards explain what's happening while your notes are copied to your phone. A long history takes a while. Wait, or tap Keep it running in the background and start using the app; the import carries on. Who are you on Nostr?, with an npub pasted Checking your relays Pasting a secret key into any app is a risk. A signer keeps the key out of Nostr Vault altogether. If you do paste it, Nostr Vault keeps it encrypted on this phone only. Who told you about Nostr Vault? If you create an account, or bring one you can post with, setup asks Who told you about Nostr Vault? It comes after Your Profile , or after Checking your relays . Read-only accounts skip it. Tap Scan their profile code , or paste their profile link or npub. Their link comes from Share profile ; see Share your profile . If you opened their link before setting up, they're already filled in. Check their profile card, and follow them. Not them? Try another goes back. Up to 10 people they follow come next, the most followed first, all ticked. Untick anyone you don't want

d: Install Nostr Vault on an Android phone, choose where your notes live, create a Nostr account or bring yours, with Amber or another signer.

A Relay You Already Run : a relay app on this phone, such as Citrine, or your own relay elsewhere, such as Nostr Vault on your Mac. Fill in Relay URL , and Blossom URL (optional) for media. Your Keys (secret key hidden here) Protect Your Key Bring the account you have Tap I already use Nostr , choose where your notes live, and the screen asks Who are you on Nostr? Paste your npub or name@domain ( Read-only ), your nsec ( You can post , and you choose a password), an ncryptsec ( Encrypted key · you can post ), or a bunker:// link ( Signer link · you can post ). Scan your key or signer link reads a QR code. Or use a signer, so your secret key never enters Nostr Vault: Use Amber shows when Amber is installed on this phone. d: Install Nostr Vault on a Mac, set it up from the menu bar, and keep your relay running while the app is open.
h: Install · Pick a way in · Create an account · Bring the account you have · Who told you about Nostr Vault? · Just look around · Find your way around · Next
x: On a Mac, Nostr Vault lives in the menu bar and runs your own Nostr relay while it's open. Leave it running and your Mac becomes the always-on home for your notes and media. Install Nostr Vault needs macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Download it from the latest release on GitHub (the NostrVault-macOS-….zip file), unzip it, and drag Nostr Vault into Applications. The first time it opens, a Welcome to Nostr Vault window says Nostr Vault lives in your menu bar . Click Get Started . Setup opens next. The first window after install Pick a way in Create an account if you're new to Nostr. I already use Nostr to bring your account, your notes and your media. Just look around to read with your public key only. The three ways in on Mac Create an account The same steps as on the iPhone: Create My Account , save your secret key on Your Keys and tick I saved my secret key , choose a password on Protect Your Key , then a photo and name on Your Profile (or Skip for Now ), and Start Exploring . The details are on Get started on iPhone . About the password on Protect Your Key : This password locks the secret key you just saved. It stays on this device only and is never sent to us or any server. We cannot recover or reset it. If you forget it, the secret key you saved is your only way back in. Bring the account you have Enter Your Keys. Pick how you sign: Private Key : paste your nsec and choose a password. The key is encrypted on this Mac. Remote Signer : Connect with Clave on your iPhone shows a code to scan with Clave. Or paste a bunker link from any signer app. Your key stays in the signer. No account yet? New to Nostr? Generate Keys makes one here. Your Personal Relay. Your relay runs on this Mac either way. A Relay Domain (optional) makes it reachable from your other devices. Leave it blank for local only, or tap Skip — configure later . Bring Your Notes Home. From Network copies your notes from public relays to this Mac; From Backup restores a Nostr Vault backup. Tap Import Notes , or Skip — I'll start fresh . Mirror Your Media. Copies your photos and videos from a Blossom media server, or from a backup, to this Mac. Tap Sync Media or Skip Media . Lightning (NWC). Paste a Nostr Wallet Connect link to send zaps, or Skip — set up later . You're All Set. Click Launch Nostr Vault . Enter Your Keys Your Personal Relay Bring Your Notes Home You're All Set Who told you about Nostr Vault? Setup with a key you can post with asks who told you about Nostr Vault, just before the last screen. Paste their profile link or npub, check their profile card and follow them, then pick from up to 10 people they follow (all ticked to start). Skip, nobody told me leaves it out. On a Mac a profile link can't fill this in for you, so paste it. Details on Get started on iPhone . Just look around Enter Your Public Key (your npub or name@domain), import your notes if you like, and Ready to Browse opens the app. Re-run setup later to post, DM and zap. Find your way around Click the Nostr Vault icon in the menu bar. The panel shows your relay's status, your notes and your media. Open Full App opens the full window, with the feed. The gear at the bottom ( Settings (⌘,) ) opens Settings. Your relay runs while Nostr Vault is open. The power button next to it ( Quit Nostr Vault ) stops it. To keep it running, open Settings → Startup and turn on Launch at Login and Start Relay Automatically . The menu bar panel Settings, Startup Next The mesh : make your Mac the photo server and vault for your phones. Your keys and accounts

t: Use Nostr Vault in a browser
d: Open the Nostr Vault web app at nostrvault.app/vault/, create an account or sign in with a browser extension, a bunker link or read-only, and know what the web app keeps in your browser.
h: New to Nostr · Sign in · Opening a shared post · Find your way around · Browsers · Your data in this browser · Next
x: The web app is Nostr Vault in a browser tab, with nothing to install. Open nostrvault.app/vault/ in any up-to-date browser, on a computer or a phone. Like the apps, it runs your own relay, here inside the browser. Your notes and messages are kept in this browser's storage. New to Nostr Click Create an account . The web app makes your keys in this browser and shows both. Save the secret key somewhere safe, tick I saved my secret key , and choose a password. Add a name and photo if you like, pick some people to follow, and click Start Exploring . The secret key stays in this browser, locked with your password; it is never sent anywhere. To see it again, open Settings → Your Secret Key and type your password. Signing out, or the browser clearing this site's data, deletes it from this browser, and nobody can recover it for you. The web app can't sign in with a secret key, so to use the account again, add the copy you saved to a Nostr browser extension and click I already use Nostr , or import it in the Nostr Vault app. Sign in Already use Nostr? Click I already use Nostr . The web app never asks for the secret key of an account you already have. Sign in with something that holds the key for you: A browser extension. If a Nostr signing extension is installed in this browser, Sign in with extension shows. Click it and approve in the extension. On iPhone and iPad, use Safari with Nostr Build Shack or Nostash . A remote signer. Paste a bunker:// link from your signer app into Bunker link (NIP-46) , click Connect bunker , and approve the connection in your signer. See Signers . Read-only. Type your name, npub or name@domain and click Find me . You can read your feed but not post. The sign-in screen in a desktop browser Accounts you've used in this browser are listed at the top next time, so one click signs you back in. Opening a shared post A post shared from Nostr Vault opens in the web app, and anyone can read it without signing in. The top says Viewing as a guest . Click Sign in there to reply, like or zap. A guest's browser keeps nothing once the tab is closed. Find your way around The same places as the phone apps: Feed , Search , Profile , WoT and Vault . On a phone they're a tab bar at the bottom; in a wide window they're a sidebar, and a post opens next to the list. Settings is the gear on your profile. Browsers The web app runs in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. On iPhone and iPad it needs iOS 16.4 or later, and on a Mac Safari 16.4 or later; keep other browsers up to date. An older browser shows a blank page. It needs WebAssembly and site storage (IndexedDB). Lockdown Mode on iPhone, iPad or Mac turns WebAssembly off, so the app says Your relay didn't start . Turn Lockdown Mode off for nostrvault.app in its web browsing settings. A private or incognito window deletes everything when it closes. Your data in this browser Your relay, notes, messages and drafts live in this browser's storage on this device, not on our server. After you sign in the app asks the browser to keep them. The Relay screen shows how much space they take and the browser's answer: Kept on this browser or This browser may clear it . Settings → Backup & Restore → Export notes saves your notes, private notes, messages and feed cache as a .zip, the same file the phone apps make. Photos and videos aren't in it. Import notes puts a .zip back into this browser, from the web or a phone. Nothing is published. Under This browser's copy , Sign out and delete this browser's copy removes everything this browser holds. Your phone's vault is untouched. Clearing your browser's site data deletes the web app's copy too. Your posts are still on public relays and in your phone or Mac vault. Safari deletes this copy after 7 days without a visit. That's every browser on iPhone and iPad, and Safari on a Mac. To keep it, add Nostr Vault to your Home Screen ( Share → Add to Home Screen ) or, on a Mac, the Dock ( File → Add to Dock ), and open it from there. Next Signers : which

d: What your Nostr keys are, where Nostr Vault keeps them, and how to add accounts, switch between them, back up your secret key and remove a key.
h: Two keys · Where to find them · Add another account · Switch accounts · Back up your secret key · Change how an account signs · Remove a key or an account · Publish Relay List · Next
x: A Nostr account is a pair of keys. Nostr Vault keeps them on your device, or leaves the secret one with a signer app, and never on a server. Two keys Public key (starts with npub ): your name on Nostr. Share it freely. With only this, an app can show your feed but can't post as you. Secret key (starts with nsec ): your password to Nostr. Anyone who has it can post as you, forever. Nobody can reset it or recover it for you, not even us. Nostr Vault can sign for you in two ways: A local key. Your secret key, locked with a password you choose (at least 8 characters), and kept on this device only. A key locked this way starts with ncryptsec . This password locks your secret key. It stays on this device only and is never sent to us or any server. We cannot recover or reset it. If you forget it, your saved secret key is your only way back in. A signer. A separate app holds your secret key and approves each post. Nostr Vault never sees the key. See Signers . Where to find them Device Open iPhone, iPad, Android Profile tab → gear → Accounts & Keys Mac Menu bar icon → gear → Accounts & Keys Web Settings → Accounts & Keys Each account shows how it signs: Local Key , Remote Signer , Amber (Android), or no signing key at all (read-only). The first account you set up is the Owner : it's the one your vault relay belongs to. Tap an account to manage it. On iPhone, iPad and Mac it opens its own page; on Android its row opens in place. Accounts & Keys on iPhone An account on iPhone An account on Android Add another account In Accounts & Keys , tap Add Account . Paste the account's key. iPhone, iPad and Mac take its npub. Then open the new account and tap Import Private Key or Connect Remote Signer to post with it. Android takes an npub, an nsec or an ncryptsec, or Connect Remote Signer (NIP-46) . Web signs in with the account's own extension or bunker. The account you're using stays signed in. Accounts & Keys on Mac Switch accounts iPhone: hold your picture in the middle of the tab bar and pick an account. It only opens when you have more than one. Mac: the account button in the menu bar panel. Everywhere: open the account in Accounts & Keys and tap Switch to This Account . A post is always sent from the account that was active when you tapped Post. Back up your secret key Do this once, right after you make an account, and keep the key in a password manager. Open the account in Accounts & Keys . Tap Reveal Key (Android: Reveal Private Key ). The app checks it's you with Face ID, Touch ID or your device passcode, then asks for the key's password. Copy the key into your password manager. Don't paste it into a chat, a note or a screenshot. Reveal Private Key, still locked With a signer, there's no key to reveal here. Back it up in the signer app. Change how an account signs Import Private Key adds a local key to an account that only had a public key or a signer. Tick Encrypt with Password to lock it. Connect Remote Signer adds a signer. It must hold this account's key; a signer for another account is refused. With both, Sign With (Android: Signing ) picks which one signs. Remove a key or an account Remove Local Key deletes the secret key from this device. If it's your only copy, it's gone for good. Disconnect Remote Signer drops the signer's connection. Reconnecting needs a fresh bunker link. Remove Account takes the account, and any key or signer for it, off this device. Nothing on the relays changes, but you need the key again to sign back in. Publish Relay List Publish Relay List tells other Nostr apps which relays you read from and write to, so they can find your posts and reach you. Your own relay is always included. Next Signers : Amber, Clave, bunker links and browser extensions.

d: Keep your Nostr secret key out of Nostr Vault with a signer: Amber on Android, Clave on iPhone, a bunker link from any signer app, or a browser extension on the web.
h: Which signer, where · Sign in with a signer during setup · Add a signer to an account you already have · On the web · Good to know
x: A signer is a separate app that holds your secret key. When Nostr Vault wants to post, like or send a message as you, it asks the signer, and the signer approves. Your key never enters Nostr Vault, so a problem in Nostr Vault can't leak it. Which signer, where Device Signers How it connects Android Amber, or any signer app on the phone Use Amber , or Use a signer app → Sign in with a signer app iPhone and iPad Clave Use a signer app → Sign in with Clave Mac Clave on your iPhone Connect with Clave on your iPhone shows a code to scan Web A Nostr browser extension. On iPhone and iPad: Nostr Build Shack or Nostash in Safari Sign in with extension Everywhere Any signer that gives a bunker link (NIP-46), such as nsec.app or your own bunker Paste or scan the bunker:// link Sign in with a signer during setup Choose I already use Nostr . On iPhone and Android, the next screen has Use a signer app under the box (and Use Amber on Android when Amber is installed). On a Mac, choose Remote Signer . The signer opens, or a code shows on screen to scan with a signer on another device. Approve the connection in the signer, then come back to Nostr Vault. If the signer didn't open, tap Open Clave again (Android: Open signer again ), or Copy link and open it yourself. Or paste a bunker:// link from any signer app into the same box. Remote Signer on Mac: Connect with Clave on your iPhone Add a signer to an account you already have Open Settings → Accounts & Keys and tap the account. Tap Connect Remote Signer . Paste the bunker link into Bunker URI , or scan its QR code. On iPhone you can Sign in with Clave here too. Approve the connection in your signer app. Connect a signer on iPhone Connect Remote Signer on Android The signer has to hold this account's key. A signer for a different account is refused. On the web An account you already have signs on the web with a signer: a browser extension, or a bunker link in Bunker link (NIP-46) and Connect bunker . It never asks for that account's secret key. (An account made with Create an account on the web keeps its key in that browser, locked with your password: see Use Nostr Vault in a browser .) A bunker's connection to the browser is stored encrypted, and removing the account or signing out asks the bunker to drop it. Good to know Posts, likes and messages are signed by the signer, which may ask you to approve each one. If nothing happens, open the signer and check for a pending request. To stop using a signer, open the account and tap Disconnect Remote Signer . Revoke the connection in the signer app too. Back up your secret key in the signer app. Nostr Vault can't show it to you, because it never has it.

d: How the Nostr Vault wallet works: connect a Lightning wallet with a Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) link, turn on zap buttons, disconnect, and the on-chain Bitcoin address under Advanced.
h: What the wallet is · Connect a wallet · Turning on zap buttons · Saving the wallet to your Nostr account · Disconnecting · Bitcoin On-Chain · The Wallet Connect tutorial
x: The basics What the wallet is A zap is a small bitcoin tip sent over Lightning (bitcoin's fast payment network) to the person who posted. Amounts are in sats , the smallest unit of bitcoin. Nostr Vault never holds that money. Your sats stay in a Lightning wallet you run somewhere else, such as Alby Hub, Coinos, Primal or Zeus. Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) is a standard way for an app to ask that wallet to pay. Your wallet gives you a link that starts with nostr+walletconnect:// , and you paste it into Nostr Vault. Treat the link like cash. Anyone who has it can spend from that wallet. If your wallet lets you, make a connection with a spending limit just for Nostr Vault. Step by step Connect a wallet In your wallet app, find Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) and copy the connection link. In Nostr Vault, open Settings → Account → Wallet . Paste the link into the Wallet Connect box (on Android it's called Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) ). On the web, tap Connect wallet . The app pastes the link only. There is no QR scanner for it. Once a wallet is connected you'll see its Balance and can set your Default Zap (on Android, Default Zap Amount (sats) ), the amount one tap sends. On iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android you can also start from your own profile. Tap the bolt, labelled Lightning . With no wallet yet, it shows No Wallet Connected and a Connect a wallet button that takes you to the same place. On Android the wallet is on the Settings tab of that screen. Once connected, the Lightning screen shows your balance and lets you receive with an invoice, pay an invoice, lightning address or LNURL, and see your history if your wallet shares it. Opt in Turning on zap buttons Zap buttons on posts are a choice you make under Settings → Appearance → Post buttons . Add ⚡️ in the Add ⚡️ field to show a zap button, and remove it to hide the button. Zapping someone from their profile is always available. iPhone, iPad and Mac: the zap button is off until you add ⚡️. It then shows on posts, live streams and locked articles. Android: ⚡️ is there by default, so posts show a zap button until you remove it. Web: notes show a zap button. A tap sends your default zap, and holding it lets you pick another amount. Turn off Zap button ⚡️ under Settings → Post buttons to hide it. Each zap goes straight from your wallet to the author. Nostr Vault takes no cut. Phones and Mac Saving the wallet to your Nostr account On iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android, the Wallet page can switch on Save wallet to my Nostr account . The link is then stored encrypted to your key on your relays, so Nostr Vault on your other devices (or the Wisp app) can pick it up with Use saved wallet . Anyone who has your Nostr key can read it and spend from the wallet. Remove from my account takes it off again. Stop using it Disconnecting iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android: delete the link from the Wallet Connect box. If you saved it to your account, also tap Remove from my account . Web: tap Disconnect wallet , then Disconnect . The web app keeps the link only in that browser, and deletes it when you sign out. To be sure the app can't spend any more, also revoke the connection in your wallet app. Advanced Bitcoin On-Chain Separate from Lightning, the apps can make a regular bitcoin address from your Nostr key. It lives under Settings → Advanced → Bitcoin On-Chain on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android. It isn't in the web app. Turn on Bitcoin Address to see the address and a QR code, and use Copy Address to share it. Sweep Wallet sends everything at that address to another address you choose. This one is different. Bitcoin sent to this address is controlled by your Nostr key, so anyone with your key can spend it. Before a sweep, the app warns you not to send to a hardware wallet or an exchange: that would tie your npub to that wallet on the public blockchain, and it can't be undone. d: Nostr Vault feeds: Following, Discover, Global, Popular, Media and the rest; Edit Feeds; the Web of Trust shield; languages; reposts, replies and auto-load; and how a new account fills its feed.
h: The feeds · Edit Feeds · Web of Trust or Everyone · The buttons at the top · New posts · Feed & Display · Spam and blocking · Filling an empty feed · On each device
x: The feeds Tap the feed name at the top left of the Feed tab to switch. On iPhone you can also hold the Feed tab and slide up. Following : people you follow. It's always on. Discover : the people your follows follow. Global : everyone in your web of trust , without replies. Hashtags : the hashtags you follow. Popular : what's getting the most replies, reposts, likes and zaps. Media : photos and videos. diVines : short looping videos. Articles : long-form posts. An edited article shows once. Recipes : recipes posted for zap.cooking. Marketplace : things for sale. Live : live streams, loaded fresh each time. Polls : polls you can vote in. Music : tracks from Wavlake. Pick yours Edit Feeds Open the feed menu and tap Edit Feeds at the bottom. Tap a feed to show or hide it. Drag a feed to move it. On Android, drag the handle. Tap Reset to Default to start over. Following can't be hidden. If you hide the feed you're on, you go back to Following. Spam stays out Web of Trust or Everyone Global, Media, Articles, diVines, Recipes, Live and Marketplace show only people in your web of trust: people you follow and the people they follow. A shield at the top right says Web of Trust . Tap it to switch to Everyone . You'll get a Sensitive Content Warning first, because Everyone is unfiltered and you should expect spam. It starts on Web of Trust. Everyone stays locked until you follow at least 5 people. Until then the shield shows a lock, and tapping it explains why: Everyone is locked , how many of the 5 you follow, and how many more to go, for example "Follow 3 more people to unlock Everyone". Follow a few people and the switch opens. If you had already turned Everyone on, it stays on. If your web isn't built yet, Global and Media stay empty instead of showing everyone. Tune a feed The buttons at the top Each feed shows the buttons that make sense for it. Reposts , Replies and Auto-load on Following, Discover and Global. These are the same switches as in Settings, so turning one off here turns it off everywhere. Languages on Global: pick one or more, or All languages . Your phone guesses each post's language. Posts too short to tell are kept. Following or Global on Media, Articles, Recipes, Marketplace, diVines and Live, to pick whose posts you see. On Popular, a menu to rank posts from everyone, only follows, or only people you don't follow. A layout button: Expanded View , Compact View or Threaded View . Each feed remembers its own. Staying current New posts When new posts arrive, a pill at the top says how many. Tap it to load them, or pull down on the feed. Turn on Auto-load to add them as they arrive. Tap the Feed tab again to jump to the top. A repost shows " name reposted" above the post. Settings Feed & Display Open Settings → Feed & Display . d: Nostr Vault messages and notifications: where Messages is, starting a message, NIP-17 and NIP-04, photos, DM relays, who can message you, the Vault activity list, notification settings and in-app pills.
h: Where your messages are · Start a message · Sending a photo · NIP-17 and NIP-04 · DM relays and who can reach you · Your notifications · Notification settings · No push server
x: Where your messages are iPhone and Android: open the Vault tab and tap the envelope at the top right. A red dot means something is unread. iPad: Messages in the sidebar, with an unread count. Mac: the Messages button on your profile. Web: Messages on the Vault tab, or in the sidebar on a computer (shortcut g m ). Write to someone Start a message In Messages, tap the compose button ( New Message ). In To:, type at least two letters of a name, or paste an npub. Write your message and tap Send. You can also tap Message on someone's profile or on their card in the WoT tab, or Message seller on a Marketplace listing, which fills in the listing for you. On the web, type a name or paste an npub and tap Open . Opening a conversation marks it read. Mark all as read is at the top of the list. Read state stays on each device. Photos Sending a photo In a conversation, tap Attach photo (Android: Attach image, web: Photo), paste one with Paste Photo , or drag it in on a Mac or iPad. The photo goes to your media server first, and its link goes in the message. Photos other than GIFs are re-saved, which removes their location. On iPhone, the New Message screen has no photo button: send the first message, then add photos in the conversation. You can select and copy text in a message on iPhone and Android. There is no way to delete a message. Encryption NIP-17 and NIP-04 Messages are sent with NIP-17 : the message is sealed and wrapped so relays can't see who it's from, who it's for, or what it says. A copy goes to you too, so your other devices see it. Some older apps only speak the older NIP-04 , which hides the text but not who's talking. Nostr Vault reads both. On iPhone and Android, the bar above the message box says NIP-17 (encrypted) ; tap Switch to send NIP-04 (legacy) in that conversation. It goes back to NIP-17 next time you open it. The web app sends NIP-17 only. If you sign with a signer app, some messages may wait for it: "N messages are waiting for your signer to open them". Open the signer, approve, and tap Retry . Where messages go DM relays and who can reach you Your DM inbox is a list of relays (the DMs column under Settings → Relays → Relays ). Other apps send your messages there. Keep at least two: with No DM relay people can't message you, and with Only one DM relay nobody can if it goes down. If your Mac is your vault, its inbox is listed first. When you send, Nostr Vault uses the other person's DM inbox, and falls back to their normal relays if they don't have one. Someone delivering straight to your vault's own inbox has to be in your web of trust . Follow Distance under Settings → Your Vault Relay → Who Can Reach You sets how far out that goes ( more ). There is no separate requests folder. Messages from people you've blocked are hidden. What happened Your notifications On iPhone and Android, the Vault tab opens on your activity: replies, mentions, quotes, likes, reposts, zaps and new followers. Likes, zaps and reposts on the same post fold into one line ("Ann and 3 others"), and new followers fold per day. Tap Mentions to see only replies, mentions and quotes. The web app has the same list under Notifications . Settings Notification settings Open Settings → Notifications . Notifications turns them all on or off. New Notes in Your Feed tells you when new posts arrive. Sound picks the alert sound. For each account: Mentions , Replies , Direct Messages , Zaps , Reactions , Reposts and New Followers . Only people in your web of trust can set off an alert. Messages, zaps and follows always come through. A new follower outside your web is counted ("3 new followers") instead of named. A message alert says who it's from. If you don't see it, the copy left in Notification Center just says "New message", without the sender or the text. How they arrive No push server Your vault makes the notifications on your phone. Nothing goes through Apple's or Google's push servers. iPhone: iOS wakes the app in the background now and then to c

d: How Nostr Vault notifications work without APNs or FCM push on iPhone, Android, Mac and the web app: what wakes the app, when alerts arrive while it is open, in the background or closed, what to allow, and the limits.
h: Why there is no push · iPhone: when iOS lets it run · Android: your vault keeps running · Mac: always on while it's running · Web: only while a tab is open
x: Why there is no push Most apps get their alerts from a company server, which hands them to Apple (APNs) or Google (FCM) to send to your phone. That server sees who wrote to you and when. Nostr Vault has no such server. The relay inside the app collects what tags you, and the app makes the notification itself on your device. So an alert can only come while that relay is running. How often it can run is different on each device. On every device: Only people in your web of trust set off an alert. New followers from outside it are counted ("3 new followers") instead of named. You choose the kinds under Settings → Notifications ( more ). Likes and reposts are off until you turn them on. While the app is open, new things show as a pill at the top, not as a system alert. Something older than 24 hours never sets off an alert. When the vault catches up after being away, the first five items alert and the rest fold into one summary. iPhone and iPad iPhone: when iOS lets it run What wakes it: iOS's Background App Refresh. The app asks to be woken every 15 minutes at the earliest. iOS decides when that actually happens, based on how often you use the app, your battery and your connection. There is also a longer check that iOS only runs while the phone is charging and online. Open: things arrive right away and show as a pill at the top. They are also listed in Notification Center. In the background: the app keeps going for about 30 seconds after you leave it, then iOS pauses it. After that, alerts come only when iOS wakes the app. That can be minutes later or much longer. Swiped away: this stops your vault. iOS may not wake an app you swiped away until you open it again, so alerts wait until then. With a Mac: if your Mac is your vault, each wake asks it for what came in while the phone was asleep. The Mac is always listening, so less is missed. What to allow: notifications (the app asks during setup), and iOS Settings → General → Background App Refresh on for Nostr Vault. The app doesn't check that second one for you. Low Power Mode pauses Background App Refresh. The honest limit: an iPhone without a Mac vault is not instant. If you need alerts right away, keep a Mac vault running or open the app. Android Android: your vault keeps running What wakes it: nothing has to. Your vault runs as a service you can see: the Nostr Vault Relay notification, which says Relay running and has a Stop Relay button. It listens to your relays all the time and checks for anything it missed every 15 minutes. Open: new things show as a pill. Pills you didn't look at are filed quietly under Missed while open . In the background or swiped away: alerts come right away, because the vault keeps running. After a restart or an app update: the vault starts again by itself, as long as Start Relay Automatically is on (it is unless you turned it off, under Settings → Your Vault Relay ). Force stopped or Stop Relay: no alerts until you open the app again. Using another app's relay (such as Citrine) instead of the built-in one: Nostr Vault makes no alerts. What to allow: notifications. On Android 13 and newer, setup asks with Enable Notifications , and turning on Settings → Notifications asks again if you said no. The honest limit: some phones' battery savers close background apps anyway, and the app doesn't ask to be left alone. If alerts stop, set Nostr Vault's battery use to Unrestricted in Android's settings. If the vault keeps failing, it stops restarting itself after four tries in six hours; opening the app starts it again. Mac Mac: always on while it's running What wakes it: nothing has to. Nostr Vault lives in the menu bar, with no Dock icon, and your vault keeps running when you close its window. It listens to your relays all the time. Running: alerts come right away, as normal Mac notifications. You won't get a banner while the Nostr Vault window is in front of you. Asleep: nothing arrives while the Mac sleeps. When it wakes, the vault catches up. Quit: no alerts

d: Nostr Vault's web of trust: the WoT tab globe, layers (Following, Vouched, Further out), Find someone, trust paths, My Web, Rebuild your web, and the Who Can Reach You settings.
h: What it is · The globe · Trust paths and their web · My Web and rebuilding · What your web decides · Who Can Reach You · On each device
x: What it is Nostr has no central moderator. Instead, Nostr Vault trusts who you trust. Your web has three rings: Following : the people you follow. Vouched : people that 10 or more of your follows follow. Further out : people your follows follow, but fewer than 10 of them. Your vault relay rebuilds the web on its own once a day. If you follow very few people, it borrows from your follows' follows so a new account isn't empty. The WoT tab The globe Open the WoT tab. You're in the middle. Your follows sit on the first ring, Vouched people on the next, and everyone else is a faint outer shell. Each person always sits in the same spot, because their place comes from their key. Layers. The menu at the top left picks Everyone , Following , Vouched or Further out , each with a count. Vouched shows up once your vault has counted your web. Filters. Talk with you keeps people you've replied to, reposted, liked or zapped, or who did that to you. Follow you back keeps follows who follow you too. Find someone. Tap the magnifier and type a name. Your follows come first, then your web, then everyone else. Why someone is here Trust paths and their web Tap a face to open their card. The line under their name says how they reach you, for example "You follow them · 1 hop" or "Followed by Ann, Bo + more you follow · 2 hops". If no one you follow follows them, it says "Not in your web". From the card you can follow or unfollow, open their Profile , or tap See their web to put them in the middle and see the globe from their side. A globe opened from a profile or a post has Open in WoT instead, which takes you to the WoT tab. A post's Event Info shows the same trust path for its author. The numbers My Web and rebuilding Tap My Web for the whole picture: how many people are in your web, how many you follow, how many are Vouched, who talks with you and who follows you back. Under Upkeep it says when the web was last rebuilt. Just followed a lot of people? Tap Rebuild your web (in My Web, or at the bottom of the layer menu). The globe shows each step: reading your follow list, reading your follows' lists, counting. A full rebuild can take a few minutes. If it fails or the vault relay isn't running, the globe keeps your last saved web. Where it's used What your web decides Who can reach your vault. Only people in your web can post to your vault's inbox. Strangers can still reply to or quote your own posts. Notifications. Replies, likes and mentions notify you only from people in your web. Zaps, follows and messages always come through. A new follower outside your web is folded into "N new followers". Feeds. Global, Media and the other discovery feeds show only your web unless you switch them to Everyone. Everyone unlocks once you follow 5 people. See Feeds . Search. Your follows and your web rank above everyone else. Mesh photos. Photos load over the mesh only from people you follow, not from your wider web. Settings Who Can Reach You On iPhone and Android, open Settings → Your Vault Relay → Who Can Reach You . Follow Distance sets how far out your web reaches (3, your whole web, to start), Minimum Followers how many of your follows must vouch for someone further out, and Refresh Trust List how often it's rebuilt. Details on Who Can Reach You . On each device iPhone, iPad and Android have everything on this page. The web app has a WoT tab with a Globe and My Web . It builds your web in the browser from follow lists, so there's no Rebuild button and no trust settings. Its search box says "Find a name, npub or key". Replay it in the app: Settings → Help → Tutorials → Your Web of Trust .

d: How Nostr Vault's mesh works: your phone or Mac serves your own photos over the FIPS mesh, with no public IP, domain or cloud. My Devices, kiosk mode, share pages and privacy.
h: What the mesh is · Your phone or Mac as your photo server · My Devices · Kiosk mode · Share pages · Privacy · What works today
x: The basics What the mesh is Most phones and home computers can't be reached from the internet. They sit behind a home router, move between Wi-Fi and cell, and have no fixed address. That's why your photos normally live on someone else's server. FIPS is a mesh network where you reach a device by its Nostr key (an npub) instead of an IP address. It works across home routers and mobile networks, and the connection between two devices is encrypted end to end. Nostr Vault uses it to let your devices reach each other, and to let other people fetch your photos from you. Photos stay trustworthy no matter who hands them over. On Nostr, a photo is named by its fingerprint (a hash). Whoever sends it, the app checks the fingerprint, and if it matches, it's the photo. If it doesn't, the photo is thrown away and loaded the normal way. Your own server Your phone or Mac as your photo server Your Nostr profile already keeps a list of where your media lives. Nostr Vault adds one more entry to that list: your Mac, or a spare phone you use as your home vault, written as its mesh address. Your everyday phone isn't listed. It goes after your normal media servers, so apps that don't know about the mesh carry on as before. An app that does know about it can ask your device for a photo directly, by its fingerprint, the same way it would ask any media server. Your photos still go to your normal servers too. Your device is one more place they can come from, and the one you own. On a Mac , the Nostr Vault app serves while it's open. Leave it running and your Mac is an always-on photo server. On a phone , it serves while the app is open, or full-time in kiosk mode on a spare phone. Step by step: your Mac as your photo server , home vault and kiosk mode . To turn it on, open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh and switch on Mesh . Serving is off until you turn it on. Your devices, together My Devices My Devices is the list of your own phones, Macs, home vault and browser page that reach each other over the mesh. Devices on this list sync with each other in full: your notes, your photos and your history. On each device, open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh , turn on Mesh , and in This Device tap Copy . That's the device's mesh address. On your other devices, go to My Devices → Add a device by address , paste it, and pick what it is: Vault on Mac , Phone or Home vault . Do it in both directions: add each phone on the Mac, and the Mac on each phone. A device on the list shows a dot when it's in reach. To check that everything arrived, use FIPS Mesh → Sync → Check sync on a phone. An always-on vault Kiosk mode Kiosk mode turns a phone into a small always-on vault. Put an old phone on a charger at home, turn kiosk mode on under Share With Others , and it keeps serving. It keeps the screen on, so the phone keeps serving. Leaving the app pauses kiosk mode, and it turns on again when you come back. Your own devices in My Devices reach it in full. Everyone else can only read the photos in your posts, and only slowly: 1 MB/s shared between all of them, at most 256 MB each, and 1 GB per session before they have to wait. They can't read your notes or change anything. Set another phone to use it as its Home vault , and your new notes and photos go to the kiosk phone over the mesh, which sends your notes on to your relays. Works in any browser Share pages When you share a post from Nostr Vault, the link opens that post in the Nostr Vault web app, in any normal browser. Anyone can read it as a guest, with no account and nothing to install, and sign in from there to reply or like. If a photo in that post or its replies can't be loaded from its usual server, the browser fetches it from that author's own device over the mesh. It joins the mesh for that one visit with a throwaway key, asks the device for the photo by its fingerprint, checks the fingerprint, and shows it. The photo is fetched by the visitor's own browser. nostrvault.app keeps no copy of it, and a guest's browser keeps no

d: Connect your iPhone, Android phone, Mac, home vault and browser page over the FIPS mesh, by address or QR code, so they sync with each other.
h: Turn the mesh on · Add a device · The list · Next
x: My Devices is the list of your own phones, Macs, home vault and browser page that reach each other over the mesh. They don't need a public IP or a domain: the mesh finds each device by its key, at home or on mobile data. Devices on the list sync with each other: your notes, your photos and your history. Anyone not on the list can only read the photos in your public posts. Turn the mesh on On each device, open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh and switch on Mesh . Under This Device you'll see its Mesh address , a long key starting with npub . That's how your other devices find this one. FIPS Mesh on iPhone FIPS Mesh on Android Add a device On the device you want to add, open FIPS Mesh and, under This Device , tap Copy , or Show QR to scan it from the other device. On the other device, tap Add a device by address . Paste the address, or tap Scan its QR code . Under This Is , pick what it is: Vault on Mac : Nostr Vault on your Mac. Your new notes and photos go to it, and your history syncs back. See Sync with your Mac . Phone : another phone of yours. Home vault : a spare phone in kiosk mode that keeps your posts. See Home vault and kiosk mode . Browser page : a Nostr Vault page in a browser that keeps a copy of your notes. Give it a name if you like, and tap Add . Do it in both directions. Add the Mac on each phone, and each phone on the Mac. A device only lets in the devices on its own list. Add a Device A device on the list You're done when both devices show each other as In reach under My Devices. It can take a moment after the mesh turns on. FIPS Mesh on Mac, with a phone in My Devices The list Each device shows In reach or Not in reach . A Mac is in reach while Nostr Vault is open on it; a phone while the app is open or in kiosk mode. Tap a device to rename it, copy its address, or remove it. On Android, What It Gets chooses whether it gets Send new notes and Send new media . Once a device is on the list, only the devices on the list learn this phone's address. Anyone else on the mesh gets public photos only. Next Sync with your Mac Remove a device, or a lost phone

d: Send each new note and photo from your phone to Nostr Vault on your Mac over the mesh, get your history back from the Mac, and check that everything arrived.
h: Set it up · Check that it arrived · Good to know
x: With your Mac on your phone's list as Vault on Mac , each new note and photo you post on the phone also goes to the Mac over the mesh. Your notes and history sync back from the Mac to the phone. The Mac becomes the second, always-on copy of your vault. Set it up Turn on the mesh on the Mac and on the phone, and add each to the other's My Devices . On the phone, pick Vault on Mac . Keep Nostr Vault open on the Mac. It syncs while it's open. Shortly after the phone's relay starts, it copies your full history from the Mac on its own. After that, new posts and mentions keep syncing by themselves. Check that it arrived On an iPhone, open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh and, under Sync , tap Check sync with Vault on Mac . On Android it's in Settings → Sync with Vault on Mac . It ends on Done with counts of what's on each side, or says why it stopped. Sync, with Check sync with Vault on Mac Copying your full history from the Mac… : the first copy is still running. Leave the app open. Copy was interrupted : the app closed during the copy. It picks up again the next time the relay starts. Send now , under Sync, sends anything that's waiting without waiting for the next post. On iPhone, the same check is also under Settings → Sync with Vault on Mac . Good to know Nothing goes through a server of ours. The phone and the Mac talk over the mesh, end to end encrypted. When the Mac is closed or out of reach, new posts still go to your public relays as usual. The Mac catches up when it's back. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. The Mac gets a copy as well.

d: Turn a spare phone into an always-on home vault with kiosk mode: it keeps your new posts and media, passes your notes on to your relays, and serves your public photos.
h: 1. Turn the spare phone into a kiosk · 2. Make it your home vault · Photos go to
x: An old phone on a charger at home can be your home vault : a small always-on copy of your vault that you own. Your main phone sends it your new posts and media over the mesh, and it passes your notes on to your relays. 1. Turn the spare phone into a kiosk Install Nostr Vault on the spare phone and sign in with the same account. Open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh , switch on Mesh , and under Share With Others switch on Kiosk mode . Leave the app open on a charger. Kiosk mode keeps the screen on so the phone keeps serving. Leaving the app pauses kiosk mode. It turns on again when you come back, and after a restart if it was on. Your devices in My Devices reach the kiosk in full. Anyone else on the mesh can read only the photos in your posts, and slowly: 1 MB/s for all of them together, at most 256 MB each, and 1 GB per session before they wait. They can't read your notes or change anything. On Android, Pause after sets how much the mesh may download before sharing pauses. Share With Others on iPhone Share With Others on Android, with Pause after 2. Make it your home vault On the kiosk phone, under This Device , copy its mesh address (or show its QR code). On your main phone, open FIPS Mesh → Add a device by address , paste or scan it, and pick Home vault . On Android, a kiosk your account already lists shows under In Your Media Servers ; tap it to use its address. Add the main phone to the kiosk's My Devices too. From then on, your new notes and media also go to the kiosk phone over the mesh, and it sends your notes on to your relays. They stay on your main phone too. Anything that can't reach it waits on the main phone and goes when the app is open and the kiosk is in reach. Send now under Sync sends it straight away. What's public. A home vault's mesh address is listed in your media server list, in public, so other apps can fetch your photos from it. Direct-message attachments are never sent there. If your key is in a remote signer, media only goes to the home vault when you tap Send now . Photos go to Under Share With Others, Photos go to ( Public server , My Mac or Both ) is where you want the photos you post to go. For now, posting a photo still needs a public media server.

t: Your Mac as your photo server
d: Let Nostr Vault on your Mac serve your photos over the FIPS mesh, listed in your media servers, with no public IP, domain or port forwarding.
h: Turn it on · Who gets what · Privacy
x: Your Nostr profile keeps a list of where your media lives. Nostr Vault on your Mac can add itself to that list, written as its mesh address. Apps that can use the mesh then load your photos straight from your Mac. Apps that can't skip it and use your other media servers, as before. Turn it on On the Mac, open Settings → FIPS Mesh and switch on Mesh . The mesh engine runs inside the Mac app; there's nothing else to install. Under Share With Others , turn on List in my media servers . Keep Nostr Vault open. In Settings → Startup , turn on Launch at Login and Start Relay Automatically so it's always there. Share With Others on Mac: List in my media servers Who gets what Your own devices in My Devices reach the Mac's vault in full. Anyone else can only open photos and files by their link, at up to 1 MB/s. They can't read your notes or change anything. Your photos still go to your normal media servers too. The Mac is one more place they can come from, and the one you own. Privacy Your home IP isn't published. The list holds the Mac's mesh key, and the mesh finds it by key. Listing it does link your npub to the Mac's mesh key, in public. Removing it later doesn't erase older copies of your list that relays may still hold. Under Advanced , Address source picks which key the listed address uses. My Nostr npub is the usual choice. More on how photos are checked on the way: The mesh .

t: Remove a device, or a lost phone
d: Take a device off My Devices so it can no longer reach your vault, and what to do when a phone with Nostr Vault is lost or stolen.
h: Remove a device · A lost or stolen phone
x: Removing a device from My Devices stops it reaching this device's vault. Do it on every device that has it on its list. Remove a device Open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh and tap the device under My Devices . On the Mac, use the remove button on its row. Tap Remove from my devices and confirm. Repeat on each of your other devices. A device on Android, with Remove from my devices What changes: It can no longer reach this device's vault, or learn its address. New notes and media stop going to it. A home vault also leaves your media server list. Anything it already has stays on it. Removing a device doesn't wipe it. A lost or stolen phone Remove it from My Devices on your Mac, your home vault and your other phones, as above. Signer: if the phone signed through a signer app, revoke its connection in the signer. Your key was never on the phone. Local key: if your secret key was on the phone, it's locked with your key password. Someone with the phone still needs that password. If you think they have it, treat the key as exposed: a Nostr key can't be changed, so make a new account and tell people to follow it. Set up the new phone : sign in with your key or signer ( iPhone , Android ), then add it to My Devices on your other devices. Your notes come back from your relays, your Mac or your home vault. Your public posts are on public relays and stay there. A lost phone loses only what nothing else holds a copy of, which is why a Mac or home vault is worth having.

t: Mesh settings: finder relays and middle server
d: What the finder relays and the middle server do in Nostr Vault's FIPS mesh settings, what they can see, and when to change them.
h: Finder Relays · Middle Server
x: Open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh → Advanced . Most people never need to change these. Changes apply the next time the mesh starts. FIPS Mesh, Advanced Finder Relays Your devices post where they are on these relays, so your other devices can find them. Like any relay, they see this device's IP address. Swipe to remove one; at least one must stay. Middle Server The middle server links two devices that can't reach each other directly. It's how this phone reaches anyone outside My Devices: the photos of people you follow, a browser page, and visitors to your kiosk. They never get this phone's address, but the middle server does see it. Which follows' photos your app loads is up to you; who can see your photos isn't a setting. Public (fips1, fips2.iris.to) : the default. None : only devices on the same network can connect. Follows' photos load from their web addresses instead, a browser page only connects on the same network, and a kiosk takes no visitors. Reset to defaults puts both lists back.

d: The Nostr Vault browser relay at nostrvault.app/relay/: a browser tab that keeps your notes and serves them to your own devices over the FIPS mesh. Pairing, Start FIPS, the screensaver, My Devices and limits.
h: What the browser relay is · Pair your iPhone with the page · What it keeps and serves · The screensaver · When the tab closes · In My Devices · Limits and privacy
x: The basics What the browser relay is A relay is a server that stores Nostr notes and hands them out. The browser relay is one that runs inside a web page, at nostrvault.app/relay/ . It stores notes in the browser's own storage on that device and joins the FIPS mesh, so your own devices can reach it by its key. New to the mesh? Read The mesh first. The page keeps no Nostr key of yours. Your notes arrive already signed, and the page checks each signature. A good spot for it is an old phone or tablet on a charger. Set it up Pair your iPhone with the page On your iPhone, open FIPS Mesh and turn the mesh on. Under This Device , tap Copy . That's the phone's mesh address. On the device that will run the page, open nostrvault.app/relay/ . Paste the address into the box under the FIPS heading (one address per line) and tap Save owners . The page reloads. Tap Start FIPS . The status shows the page's own mesh address . Copy it. On the iPhone, go to My Devices → Add a device by address , paste the page's address, and pick Browser page . The phone then connects for the page. If it doesn't, open the page's entry in My Devices and tap Connect this phone . Copy this phone's mesh address is there too. A link of the form nostrvault.app/relay/#owner=npub1 also adds an owner. The page asks you to confirm each address first, because an owner can write to the page and read everything on it. Only accept your own. What it does What it keeps and serves Your new notes. While the iPhone app is open, each new note you post also goes to the page. Send my latest notes sends your 20 most recent notes from the phone. The result line says how many the page kept. In this testing build, check that number: if it says 0 kept, the page did not take your notes. Checked notes only. The page checks each note's signature and turns away notes from authors it isn't set up for. Owners only. The page serves notes on the mesh only to the addresses saved as owners. Anyone else's connection is dropped without an answer. Photos, read only. Under Show photo , you can paste a photo's fingerprint (sha256) or a .fips link and the page fetches it from a paired vault. It shows the photo only if the fingerprint matches. Photos aren't stored on the page. The page reaches your phone through the public mesh entry points (seeds). Once both ends are connected it tries a direct link. On the iPhone, leave the middle server under Advanced on its public setting. With None , a browser page only connects on the same network. Keep it awake The screensaver Start screensaver fills the screen with a black "relay running" view: a count, the uptime, whether the screen is kept awake (the wake lock), and whether the seed is up. Tap anywhere to leave it. After a reload, start it again. The count on this screen is the page's own test notes, not your notes. Report shows storage, uptime gaps and a signature self-test, if you want the details. When it stops When the tab closes The relay only runs while the page is open and the screen is on. Closed, locked or in the background, nothing reaches it. Notes the phone sends while the page is down are not queued. Tap Send my latest notes once it's back. Stored notes stay in the browser and are there when you reopen the page. Tap Start FIPS again; it doesn't start by itself. Stop FIPS takes the page off the mesh. The page's mesh key lives in the browser's site data. Clear that data and the page gets a new address, so pair it again. Your devices list In My Devices The page shows up in My Devices as a Browser page , the role whose job reads "Gets your new notes while this app is open." You can have one browser page per account; adding a new one replaces the old. To stop sending, open its entry and tap Remove from my devices . Anything already on the page stays there.
