d: What the Nostr Vault vault relay keeps on your phone or Mac: your notes, mentions, messages and media. The Vault tab, starting and stopping it, Import Notes, and the Mac and web differences.
h: What your vault is · The Vault tab · Vault settings · Import your past notes · Phone, Mac and web
x: The basics What your vault is Most Nostr apps only read and write to other people's relays. Nostr Vault also runs one on your device. Your vault is a personal Nostr relay and a Blossom media server, and it keeps a copy of: Your own notes , everything you post, like, zap and save. Notes that mention you , from people you trust (see Who Can Reach You ). Your direct messages , still encrypted. Recent notes from people you follow , so your feed loads fast. Older ones are cleared out over time. Your media , in its Blossom media server. The vault's address ( ws://127.0.0.1: ) only works on that device, so nobody else can connect to it. Your notes still go to your normal relays too. The vault is the copy you own. To see it explained in the app, open Settings → Help → Tutorials and play Vault in Your Pocket or How Your Vault Works . iPhone and Android The Vault tab The Vault tab shows how your vault is doing. At the top it says Your vault is running , starting, paused or needs a restart, with how long it's been up. If it stops, a button lets you start it again so it catches up on new notes and messages. The menu on that card has Copy Address , Restart , Stop and Start . Below that: Who can reach you : how many people can send to your inbox. In your vault : how many events it holds and how much space notes, media and cache use. The cache is other people's media kept for quick loading, and you can clear it. Keep it full : Import notes , import media, back up media and export notes. Vault settings : shortcuts to Relays, Who Can Reach You, Media Servers and starting automatically. On Android the same screen is called Vault Dashboard . Settings Vault settings Everything about the vault is grouped under Settings → Your Vault Relay . The card at the top of Settings shows whether it's running, with a Start Relay button if it isn't. Start Relay Automatically : start the vault when the app opens. Leave it on. Sync with Vault on Mac : send your notes and photos to Nostr Vault on your Mac (see The mesh ). Who Can Reach You : who may send to your inbox and messages. More . Import Notes : fill the vault with your past notes. See below. Backup & Restore : save or restore your vault as a file. More . Bring your history Import your past notes A new vault starts empty. Import Notes pulls your old notes, and notes where you are tagged, from your other relays into the vault, starting at a date you pick. Open Settings → Your Vault Relay → Import Notes and set the Start Date . On iPhone, run it from the Vault tab: Keep it full → Import notes . On Android, tap Start Import on the same page. It reads from the relays that have Import switched on in Settings → Relays . Notes that tag you are kept only if they come from people you trust, or if they reply to or quote your own posts. Where it runs Phone, Mac and web Where the vault runs What's different iPhone Inside the app Vault tab with the full dashboard. Android Inside the app Same as iPhone; the dashboard is called Vault Dashboard. Mac Inside the menu bar app A simpler Relay Dashboard. Domain & Port lets you give the vault your own domain so your other devices can reach it, and Startup has Launch at Login . Web In your browser's storage No relay settings. Import with Import from my relays . Signing out deletes this browser's copy; your phone's vault is untouched. A vault on the web is a copy, not a backup. It lives in that browser. Use Sign out and delete this browser's copy on a shared computer, and keep real backups with Backup & Restore .

d: Nostr Vault's Who Can Reach You settings: Follow Distance, Minimum Followers and Refresh Trust List decide which people can send to your vault's inbox and messages. Spam control by Web of Trust.
h: What it controls · Follow Distance, Minimum Followers, Refresh Trust List · Who can see what · Phone, Mac and web
x: The basics What it controls Your vault has an inbox, where notes that mention you land, and a chat store for your direct messages. Anyone on Nostr can try to send to them. Who Can Reach You keeps out everyone who isn't close to you in your follows. This is your Web of Trust, and it's the vault's spam filter. Mentions and messages from people outside your trust list are turned away. Replies and quotes of your own posts still get in, from anyone. Your messages can only be read by people on the list who sign in. Your own notes aren't affected. You can always post. Open it from Settings → Your Vault Relay → Who Can Reach You , or tap Who can reach you on the Vault tab, which shows how many people can reach your inbox right now. The settings Follow Distance, Minimum Followers, Refresh Trust List Follow Distance How many follows away someone can be and still reach you. Lower is more private. Distance Who can reach you 1 Only you. 2 You and the people you follow. 3 (default) You, the people you follow, and the people they follow, if enough of your follows follow them (see Minimum Followers). The control stops at 3. An older setting of 4 or 5 shows as 3, which is how the relay always ran it. Minimum Followers At distance 3, how many of the people you follow must also follow someone before they can reach you. The default is 3. Raise it to keep out more strangers, lower it to let more friends of friends in. It has no effect at distance 1 or 2. Refresh Trust List How often the vault rebuilds the list from your follows: Every hour , Every 12 hours , Every day (default) or Every week . Someone you just followed can reach you after the next rebuild. At a glance Who can see what There's no setting for who can see your vault. This is what each kind of visitor gets. Your devices Anyone on the mesh Anyone on the web Notes Yes No Yes, your public notes Private notes Yes No No, only you Photos Yes Only photos named in your public notes Yes, your public photos Messages Yes No Only people who sign in and are within your Follow Distance Your devices are the ones in My Devices . Where to find it Phone, Mac and web iPhone and Mac have the same screen. On the Mac it's in the Settings sidebar. Android has the same settings, and restarts the vault for you when you change one. The web has no trust settings. Its Who Can Reach You row opens the browser relay's mesh panel, where Who can reach this relay is a list of your own vaults' mesh addresses. Not getting a mention you expected? The sender may be too far from you. Follow them, or raise Follow Distance, then wait for the next trust list refresh.

d: How to back up and restore Nostr Vault: export and import notes and media in Backup & Restore, restore an old follow list from Following Backup, un-delete posts in Recently Deleted, and the web backup.
h: Backup & Restore · Following Backup · Recently Deleted · Backups on the web
x: Notes and media Backup & Restore Open Settings → Your Vault Relay → Backup & Restore . It has two parts, and each one is its own file. Notes. Export Notes saves everything in your vault as a .zip: your notes, private notes, messages (still encrypted), the notes that mention you and your feed cache. Import Notes puts a notes backup back. Media. Export Media saves the photos and videos in your vault's media server as a .zip. Import Media puts them back. On iPhone the file goes to the share sheet, so you can save it to Files or send it to your Mac. On the Mac and Android you pick where to save it. A restore adds to what's already in the vault. Anything it already has is skipped, and nothing is deleted. The vault pauses for a moment while notes are saved or restored. Your keys are not in the backup. A backup holds notes and media only. Keep your key (or your signer) safe on its own; see Accounts & Keys in the app. On iPhone and Mac, start the vault before you export media. On iPhone and Android, the Vault tab has the same exports under Keep it full : Export notes and Back up media . Your follow list Following Backup A follow list on Nostr is one list that gets replaced every time it changes. A buggy app can wipe it. Nostr Vault keeps a snapshot each time your list changes, up to 50, on your device. Open Settings → Following Backup . Pick a snapshot. It shows who you no longer follow and who was added since. You can re-follow one person, or tap Restore This List to put the whole list back. Confirm. The restored list replaces your current one and is published to your relays. If your list was wiped somewhere else, Scan Relays looks for older copies of it on your relays. Undo a delete Recently Deleted Posts you delete on a device stay in Settings → Recently Deleted on that device for 30 days. Un-delete posts it again as a new post. Likes and replies on the old post don't come back. Delete Forever removes the copy now. Profiles and lists aren't kept here. Recently Deleted is in the apps and the web app. In the browser Backups on the web The web app keeps its vault in your browser, so back it up if it holds anything you don't have elsewhere. Settings → Backup & Restore : Export notes saves your notes, private notes, messages and feed cache as the same .zip the phone apps make, so either one restores the other. Photos and videos aren't in it. Import notes reads that .zip back. It also reads a .jsonl backup from an older web app. Nothing is published either way. Notes Media Follow snapshots Recently Deleted iPhone .zip .zip Yes Yes Android .zip .zip Yes Yes Mac .zip .zip Yes Yes Web .zip No Yes Yes

d: Media servers (Blossom) in Nostr Vault: where photos go when you post, adding and removing servers, mirroring copies back to your device, the Media & Cache settings, and uploading from the share sheet.
h: What a media server is · Where a photo goes when you post · Add or remove a media server · Mirroring · Media & Cache · Uploading from the share sheet · Your device as a photo server
x: The basics What a media server is Relays only carry text. A photo or video is too big for that, so it goes to a media server instead, and your note holds a link to it. Nostr media servers speak a shared language called Blossom , so any Nostr app can read from them. A photo on a Blossom server is named by its fingerprint (a hash of the file). The same photo has the same name on every server, so it can be copied between servers and still be checked. Your account publishes a list of your media servers. Other apps read that list to find your files. When you post Where a photo goes when you post The app first saves the photo on this device, in your vault. It then uploads it to all of your outside media servers at once. As soon as one of them has it, the note is sent. The other servers keep uploading in the background. If no outside server takes the photo, the post is not lost. It waits under Settings → Media Servers in Waiting to send , and sends itself when a server answers. Tap Try sending now to retry straight away. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. A photo that is only on your phone can't be seen by anyone else, so the app won't post it without an outside server. Your list Add or remove a media server Open Settings → Media Servers . It sits in the Relays group, under Relays. Add: type the server's address (for example blossom.example.com ) in the box and tap the add button next to it. If you leave out https:// , the app adds it. Remove: tap the red button next to a server (a minus sign on iPhone and Mac, a bin on Android). Each change is saved and your updated list is published to your relays. If you set up Sync with Vault on Mac , your Mac is used as a media server too. It shows at the top of the page and you don't need to add it by hand. In the web app , the same page is Settings → Media Servers . Use Add and Remove , then Save and publish . Test checks that a saved server answers. The web app uploads to the server marked first first. If you have never published a list, it starts from two default servers. It also needs at least one server in the list. There is no button to reorder servers. In the web app, a server you add goes to the end of the list. Copies you own Mirroring Mirroring brings your own photos back from your media servers into your vault on this device, so they work offline and you keep a copy if a server goes away. Both controls are on the Media Servers page: Mirror Now downloads your media from your outside servers to this device, once. It shows progress while it runs. Auto-Mirror Media keeps doing it for you. Other people's photos Media & Cache When you look at photos and videos in the feed, the app keeps temporary copies so they load faster next time. You control this in Settings → Media & Cache , in the Feed & Display group. The web app doesn't have this page. Autoplay Videos plays videos as you scroll. Prefetch Profile Pictures loads profile pictures ahead of time for smoother scrolling. Disable Media Cache stops saving copies, so media downloads again each time. Keep Media For sets how long copies are kept: 1, 3, 7, 14 or 30 days, or Never. Clear Media Cache deletes the temporary copies to free space. Your vault and your media servers are not touched. On Android there is one more switch, Use Local Blossom Cache . It loads media through a Blossom cache app on the same phone, when one is running. Uploads never go through it. From other apps Uploading from the share sheet You can send photos and videos to Nostr Vault from your gallery or any other app, using the system share button. The two phones handle it differently: Phone What happens Android Pick Nostr Vault in the share sheet. The upload to Blossom starts straight away, one file at a time, with a notification while it runs. iPhone Pick Nostr Vault, then tap Add to Blossom upload queue . The files are added to a queue. Open Nostr Vault or tap its notification to finish the upload. On iPhone the upload happens in the app, not in the shar

d: How Nostr Vault share links work: Share and Copy Link make a nostrvault.app/thread/ link that opens the post in any browser as a guest, with a link preview card. Plus sharing photos into the app.
h: Share or copy a link · The link preview · Opening a link, with or without an account · Sharing photos into Nostr Vault
x: Sharing a post Share or copy a link Open the menu on any post. Share opens your phone's share sheet, so you can send the link in a message, an email or another app. On Android it's titled Share Note . Copy Link (Android and web: Copy link ) puts the link on your clipboard and shows Link copied . The link looks like https://nostrvault.app/thread/nevent1 . The nevent part names the post and its author, so the link works without any account and doesn't depend on one relay. Articles, videos and other posts have a Share button too, and give the same kind of link. In a chat or a feed The link preview When you paste the link in a chat app or a social site, it shows a preview card: the author's name (" on Nostr"), the start of the post, and the photo if the post has one. What they see Opening a link, with or without an account The link opens the post in the Nostr Vault web app, in any normal browser. No account? They read the post and its replies as a guest. A bar at the top says Viewing as a guest , with Get the app and Sign in . They can open profiles and hashtags and come back to the post. Want to reply or like? Liking, replying, reposting and zapping need them to sign in. After signing in, the web app opens on the same post. Already signed in to the web app in that browser? The post opens in their account. A guest visit keeps nothing. Nothing is signed, and nothing is saved in the browser once the tab is closed. Photos load from their usual media server. If one can't be loaded there, the browser fetches it from the author's own device over the mesh. See The mesh . Deleted posts. If the author deletes the post, the link says This post was deleted by its author. Anyone who already saw it may still have a copy, as with anything you post publicly on Nostr. The other direction Sharing photos into Nostr Vault You can also send photos and videos from your Photos app or gallery to Nostr Vault, to upload them to your media server (Blossom). iPhone: pick up to 20 photos and 20 videos, tap Share, choose Nostr Vault, then Add to Blossom upload queue . Open Nostr Vault, or tap the Ready to upload to Blossom notification, to finish the upload. Android: share one or more photos or videos to Nostr Vault. The upload starts right away and shows Uploading to Blossom . Set up your account first. Uploading needs a public media server; see Settings → Relays → Media Servers .

d: Share profile in Nostr Vault: a QR code and a nostrvault.app/p/ link for any profile, Copy link and Share, and what happens when someone scans or opens the link.
h: Open the share sheet · Opening a profile link · Who told you about Nostr Vault? · On each device
x: Share profile Open the share sheet Your own profile: tap the QR code button next to Edit Profile . Anyone else's profile: open the menu and tap Share profile . The sheet shows a large QR code with the person's name and picture, and three ways to pass it on: Show the code. Someone points a phone camera, or the scanner in Nostr Vault, at it. Copy link puts the link on your clipboard and says Copied . Share opens the system share sheet, so you can send the link in a message, an email or another app. The link looks like https://nostrvault.app/p/npub1 . It carries only the public key, never a secret key. The other side Opening a profile link Scanned or pasted in Nostr Vault. The code from the setup scanner, or a link pasted into Search , opens the profile straight away. Search also takes a bare npub, an nprofile or a nostr: link. Opened in a browser (a tapped link, or a code scanned with the phone camera). The page shows the profile's name, picture and bio, with Open in Nostr Vault to jump into the app, Get Nostr Vault if they don't have it, and Open in another Nostr app . New to Nostr Vault? If they open the link and then install and set up the app, the person who shared it is already filled in on the Who told you about Nostr Vault? step. See below . During setup Who told you about Nostr Vault? A new account starts with an empty feed. One setup step fixes that with the person who brought you here. Tap Scan their profile code , or paste their profile link or npub and continue. Tap Skip, nobody told me to leave the step out. Their profile card shows, so you can check it's them. Tap Follow with their name, or Not them? Try another . Next come up to 10 people they follow, the ones most followed by their other follows first, all ticked. Untick anyone you'd rather not follow. Tap the button that says how many you'll follow. You follow them and everyone still ticked, as one follow list, once setup finishes. The step comes after your profile when you create an account, and after the relay check when you bring an account you can post with. Read-only accounts skip it. Details for each device: iPhone , Android , Mac . On each device iPhone, iPad and Android have everything on this page. A profile link opened before setup fills in the Who told you step. Mac has Share profile, and a link pasted into Search opens the profile. Links don't open the Mac app from a browser, so paste the link into the Who told you step yourself.

d: Fixes for common Nostr Vault problems: empty feed, signer not answering, read-only account, photo posts failing, relays not answering, mesh devices not in reach, Check sync stopping, kiosk mode paused.
h: My feed is empty · I can't post, like or follow · My signer never answers · My photo post didn't send · A relay isn't answering · Android: my vault went quiet after an update · A device on My Devices is never in reach · Check sync stops early · Someone's photos don't load over the mesh · Kiosk mode paused · Still stuck?
x: My feed is empty You see "No Following Feed". Nostr has no algorithm, so a new account starts with nothing: you see posts from people you follow. Fix: follow a few people. Fill Your Feed helps you find them by topic, and five follows builds your web of trust, which fills Discover and Global too. Replay it from Settings → Help → Tutorials . More on Feeds . Global and Media also stay empty until your web is built. That's on purpose: they show nothing rather than everyone. I can't post, like or follow You see "Read-only for now", "No private key stored for this account" or "This account is read-only. Add its key to follow." You signed in with an npub or a name@domain, which lets you look but not sign. Fix: add the account's key or connect a signer in Settings → Accounts & Keys . My signer never answers You see "Your signer didn't answer in time", "Clave didn't answer" or, on Android, "Amber signing was cancelled or timed out". Your signer app has a request waiting that you haven't approved, or it can't reach its relay. Fix: open the signer app, approve the pending request, then tap Retry in Nostr Vault. If it says "Couldn't reach your signer's relay", check your connection. "This signer is for a different account" means the signer holds another key than the account you picked. My photo post didn't send You see "Your post wasn't sent: no outside media server is set up". A photo has to sit on a public media server so other people can see it, even with the mesh. Fix: add a server in Settings → Relays → Media Servers , then post again. (Android's message says "Settings → Blossom"; the row is called Media Servers.) If it says your Mac didn't take the photo, check that Nostr Vault is open on your Mac. "Saved on this device" means the post will send itself as soon as the server answers. A relay isn't answering In the relay list you see " relay isn't answering". It didn't answer just now. Relays go down. Fix: leave it a while. If it stays down, remove it. "No Write relay" means none of your relays is set to Write, so your posts have nowhere to go: mark at least one as Write. Android: my vault went quiet after an update Installing an update stops the app, and with it your vault relay. Fix: open the app once after updating. Keep Start Relay Automatically on: newer builds then start the relay again by themselves after an update. A device on My Devices is never in reach Under Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh → My Devices a device stays "Not in reach" (Android shows when it was last seen). A Mac or a kiosk phone only answers devices that are on its own My Devices list, and a Mac with an empty list doesn't start the mesh at all. Fix: add the devices both ways. On each device, copy the address under This Device and add it on the other one; on your phones, add the Mac as Vault on Mac . Check that Mesh is on, on both. See My Devices . Check sync stops early On iPhone, Check sync with Vault on Mac ends on "Stopped · N still missing", "Copy didn't finish" with a reason, or "Copy was interrupted". The button is greyed out while a copy is running or when your vault relay isn't running. Fix: read the reason line. "Copy was interrupted" means the app closed during the copy; it picks up again the next time the relay starts. Anything that couldn't be copied is tried again once a day, and tapping the button starts a new run. Someone's photos don't load over the mesh Your app only asks the mesh for photos from people you follow, and only if they list their own vault as a media server. Files over 32 MB always come from the normal web address. This is about whose photos your app loads. It doesn't change who can see yours. Fix: follow them, and check they have the mesh turned on. Otherwise the photo loads from its web address as usual. Kiosk mode paused On iPhone you get "Kiosk mode paused". Leaving the app pauses kiosk mode. Fix: tap the notification or open the app again; kiosk mode turns back on by itself. If it won't start, add your other phone or your Mac und

d: Nostr Vault FAQ: which version is current, can I use my existing Nostr account, do I need a Mac, is my home IP public, who can see my photos, losing a phone, what the web app does, is it free.
h: Which version is current? · Is it free? Is it open source? · What is the vault? · Can I use my existing Nostr account? · Do I need a Mac? · Why does posting a photo still need a server? · Is my home IP public? · Who can see my photos over the mesh? · What if I lose my phone? · What can the web app do?
x: Which version is current? 3.0 on iPhone, Mac and Android. It adds the mesh, which connects your own devices directly. These pages describe 3.0. Is it free? Is it open source? Yes to both. The app is free and the code is MIT licensed, on GitHub . What is the vault? Your vault is a personal Nostr relay and a media server, running on your phone. It keeps your notes, your messages and your photos on the device. Nobody on the network can connect to it, unless you share it with your own devices over the mesh. Can I use my existing Nostr account? Yes. Tap I already use Nostr instead of Create an account . iPhone and Mac: paste your nsec, an encrypted key (ncryptsec) or a bunker link, or Use a signer app and Sign in with Clave . Android: paste a key or bunker link, Use Amber , or Use a signer app . Web: Sign in with extension or Connect bunker . The web app never takes your nsec. An npub or name@domain also works, read-only: you can look around but not post. Do I need a Mac? No. Your phone runs its own vault. A Mac is an optional extra: as Vault on Mac it can hold a full copy and serve your photos while it's on. A spare phone in Kiosk mode can do the same job. Why does posting a photo still need a server? Other people need to be able to see it, from any app, whether or not your phone is on. So a photo you post also goes to a public media server. The mesh is an extra, faster place to fetch it from, not a replacement. If posting fails . Is my home IP public? No. Once you add a device, only your own devices learn your phone's address. Anyone else gets your public photos and never your address, but the mesh's middle server does see it. You can change or turn off the middle server under the mesh's Advanced settings. Who can see my photos over the mesh? Your own devices get everything. Anyone else gets only photos that are in your posts, and only within limits: 1 MB/s in total, 1 GB per session and 256 MB per file. Nobody else can read your notes. Your posted photos are on public media servers too, so treat them as public. What if I lose my phone? On each of your other devices, open the lost phone under My Devices and tap Remove from my devices . The mesh restarts and the lost phone is cut off at once. The phone's mesh address is its own key, not your Nostr key. Your Nostr account is your key. Keep a copy of it somewhere safe before you need it: Settings → Accounts & Keys → Reveal Key . What can the web app do? The web app at nostrvault.app/vault/ reads your feeds, posts, including photos, and has a WoT tab. It signs in only with a browser extension, a bunker or read-only. It keeps a copy of your notes in the browser, which the browser may clear; your phone's vault is the real one. It doesn't have Edit Feeds or the trust settings.

d: Nostr Vault release notes for iPhone, Mac and Android: 3.0.0 with the FIPS mesh, and the earlier 2.7.2 builds.
x: Build 41 · iPhone, Mac and Android 3.0.0 Nostr Vault 3.0 connects your own devices directly over the FIPS mesh , with no server in between. Your devices, connected. Turn on FIPS Mesh in Settings and add your devices by address or QR code. On Android you can add your Mac, your other phones or a home vault. See My Devices . iPhone and Mac: the mesh engine runs inside the Mac app, so there is nothing else to install. The Mac serves your photos to your own devices, and your public photos to anyone else who asks. See your own photo server . Notes and photos to your Mac. Add your Mac as Vault on Mac and each new note and photo goes to it over the mesh. Your notes and history also sync back from the Mac. iPhone and Mac: Check sync with Vault on Mac now ends on "Done" with counts, or says why it stopped. Home vault. A spare phone can be your home vault. It gets your new posts and media and passes them on. See kiosk mode . Photos over the mesh. Photos kept on your devices load over the mesh in the feed, the Vault and profiles. Your address stays private. Once you add a device, only your devices learn this phone's address. Anyone else gets public photos only. On Android, that is up to the limit you set under Pause after . See privacy . Android: if the mesh was on, it starts again with the relay when the phone restarts. Fixes iPhone: the phone ran hot with the app open. The relay now gets memory sized to the phone. iPhone and Mac: search no longer freezes while you type a common word. Android: on some phones the app ran out of memory and closed when a long note full of links was in the feed. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. Build 40 · iPhone, Mac and Android 2.7.2 (build 40) iPhone and Mac. This is the App Store build. The app now stays cool with it open all day. The relay pauses work nobody can see while the app is in the background, and backs off from flaky relays and signers. The Web of Trust globe draws more cheaply. On the iPhone, a locked article no longer links out to buy it on Fanfares. The Mac keeps that link. On both, it can only point at the article itself. New Message from a profile keeps the person you picked. Android. Android now looks and acts like the iPhone app. Messages and notifications, Settings, the tab bar, setup, profiles, search, follow lists, the Web of Trust globe, the feed, note details and the composer have all been matched to the iPhone. The app runs cooler. The relay pauses work nobody can see while the app is in the background, and backs off from flaky relays. A crash at launch on a new install is fixed. d: How another Nostr client can read photos over the FIPS mesh: the fipsmesh:// address form in kind 10063, plain Blossom GETs, and the NIP-F1 draft.
x: The mesh address is one new entry form, fipsmesh://<npub>/ , in lists you already use: the media server list ( kind:10063 ) and, later, the relay list ( kind:10002 ). No new event kinds. Requests are plain Blossom GET /<sha256> , with the same hash check. A client that doesn't know the form skips it and carries on with the other servers in the list. A client that does can ask the device for the photo by its fingerprint, the same way it asks any media server, and throws the photo away if the fingerprint doesn't match. Draft, not yet submitted NIP-F1: Nostr over the FIPS Mesh The address form, transport, safety rules for serving and reading, and where Nostr Vault implements each part.
